limitations: Ribbon KRCO color tracks are read and written by MDX/MDL and published as UV_game_effects sequenceAnimation.color, including interpolation, tangents and global clocks. Their independent static color fallback survives native/UVM reconstruction as well. The native reconstruction path preserves ribbon gravity; nonzero gravity not projected to the common frame is reported. Falling-ribbon and native visual fidelity remain unqualified.

Crystal shader ID 24 and Shader_HD_Crystal are refused at model projection: no faithful common material is available, and ordinary HD is not substituted. Native parsing/re-emission is not proof of Crystal rendering.

HD Fresnel RGB and gain/Fresnel track keys survive BlizzardMDX residual reconstruction, including interpolation, tangents and global-sequence ids. The independent static KMTE gain header survives MDX write and native residual reconstruction through an admitted finite exact float32 carrier (negative zero/nonfinite/unrepresentable carriers refuse). Missing legacy carriers keep compatibility default 1, not a recovered authored header. MDL output refuses a non-default static header alongside KMTE before publication; native scalar-plus-track grammar and adjacent Fresnel static-header preservation remain unqualified. Native preservation is separate from rendering: animated emissive gain and the native Fresnel equation do not yet have a qualified common projection.

Decodes MDX and MDL geometry, materials and texture layers, bones and pivots, sequences with their node translation/rotation/scaling channels, and bounds through the vendored war3-model parser. Up to four UV sets survive the common geometry and UVM/native round-trip; CoordId selects the authored set. HD baked AO reads UV1 only with the native 0x400 flag. More than four sets, malformed UV counts, or a layer referencing an absent UV set (including AO without UV1) are refused rather than rendered with guessed coordinates.

Attachments, collision shapes, particle and ribbon emitters, cameras and lights are published as model facets. Attachment names are carried verbatim because scripts reference them; no socket orientation is claimed because Warcraft III declares neither a forward nor an up axis for one. A camera is not a node of the hierarchy, so its position and target stay in its properties.

Hermite and Bezier animation tracks are published as cubic-spline with each key's derivative per second (a Hermite tangent over the key interval, a Bezier control point as 3·(control − value)), and reach UVM as glTF CUBICSPLINE; linear and step tracks state theirs.

Replaceable texture ids (team colour, team glow, tileset trees) resolve to their canonical Warcraft III paths; opening any texture stays the host resource route's job. Explicit ATCH/PRE1 model paths publish reference-only sidecar resources with authored spelling; this does not imply binding or nested-model playback.

Installed Warcraft III is found by discovery: Reforged by its CASC build record, a classic 1.x installation by war3.mpq beside its runtime. The shipped models of a classic installation open inside its MPQ archives through blizzard/mpq, with the textures they name; the real test tier reads them from the installation discovery finds.

model.export-uvm emits UVM without UV_source_blob: geometry, materials, skeleton bindings, animation clips and the logical texture closure use common glTF/UVM structures; emitters go to UV_game_effects in the common vocabulary with sequence-local tracks, and BlizzardMDX keeps only native reconstruction facts. A request may state metersPerSourceUnit; without one a Warcraft III world unit is 0.35 m (owner decision 2026-09-23).

model.write re-emits the decoded model as MDX or MDL and verifies the result by reopening it. The separate common.model/native-encoder provider writes a Warcraft III model back from UVM, including emitter tracks placed in their sequences.

Vertex skinning exports through the portable four-weight skin. Warcraft III matrix groups larger than four influences were already capped at four by the decode, and that cap is carried rather than corrected here.

Emitter parameters are published in Warcraft III's own words and emitter simulation is not performed. PRE2 ReplaceableId, priority plane and Unshaded select its UVM sprite material. Source-free native reconstruction preserves static one-pass surface priority/Unshaded and qualified WC3 particle metadata ReplaceableId/SortPrimsFarZ/Unfogged; animated, multi-pass, non-surface or unrepresentable values refuse. Common lineEmitter/modelSpace/xyQuad restore their native bits while head/tail/squirt remain intact. SortPrimsFarZ is stored, not implemented as a sorting policy; common lighting/fog and visual fidelity remain unqualified. An emitter track on a global sequence crosses model.export-uvm as a concurrent track of every sequence that wraps at the global sequence's length, and the writer turns it back into one global sequence; an emitter rides its own node, with its pivot and tracks.
